eligibility.evidence: Sec 3.1-3.4: 40 peer-reviewed policy-evaluation findings posed as YES/NO or direction questions to four LLMs under five prompt strategies. Only a framing from dual-process theory (Sec 3.2) and one anchoring-inspired adversarial prompt (P5); no cognitive-experimental paradigm administered.

A.title: Thinking Fast, Thinking Wrong: Intuitiveness Modulates LLM Counterfactual Reasoning in Policy Evaluation

G.notes: Borderline: dual-process framing and a P5 adversarial-anchoring prompt, but items are policy-finding questions scored against published results, not a cognitive paradigm. Intuitiveness labels by one author, annotator kappa 0.32. Single independent author.
